prize_parts.citation: For a visionary Romanian-language prose oeuvre, rooted in a poet's attention to the sentence, in which memory, the body and dream are built into recursive metaphysical architectures of rare formal ambition and imaginative depth.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: Mircea Cărtărescu (B006) as the single credited name in one prize part. What changed after the exchange is the wording of the citation, not the choice. I now centre the citation on the prose project and its formal architecture. The poetry appears only as the origin of the sentence-level texture. This follows the chair's question on scope, and I think it is the most defensible position. Public knowledge of Blinding, the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy, and of Solenoid describes a voice that is hard to mistake for another writer's. Memory, the body, dream and cosmology are joined in large recursive structures, so the claim is about construction as well as imagery. That is the sense in which I read the late work as an escalation of scale and structure rather than a restatement. I hold this as a judgment from public knowledge and shortlist descriptions, not from verified reading of the whole corpus. Under the common criteria it gives the clearest whole-oeuvre claim on the shortlist: distinctiveness of voice, formal ambition, imaginative and intellectual depth, and a sustained project. The agreement among all six round-1 files is not evidence of merit, and I have not used it as such. The case rests on the literary reasoning above.
statement.case_against: The reservation I cannot remove is that I am judging the density, rhythm and syntax of Romanian prose through translation and secondary description. Maximalist, recursive books can enlarge a project or only restate it, and length alone does not show sustained quality. The chair asked which passages or volumes should settle this. I cannot name specific passages without fabricating, and I have not verified the corpus. If the committee's readers concluded that the later long works restate the Orbitor motifs without deepening them, my view of the whole-oeuvre claim would weaken. Adonis would then have the stronger claim on linguistic renewal of a major literary tradition. A second reservation is that excluding the poetry from the citation may undersell the oeuvre, but I would accept that cost rather than claim coverage I cannot assess.

responses.point: Carlberg's round-1 citation names a prose and poetic oeuvre. The chair summary records that she would include the poetry, and she also accepts that coverage of the poetry and early work in translation is uneven.
responses.response: I would narrow the citation. The poetry matters as the source of the sentence-level texture, but its translation coverage is the thinnest part of the corpus, so a citation naming it claims more than I can assess. I would write 'rooted in a poet's attention to the sentence' and rest the claim on the prose project. This is a difference in what we can defend, not in how we value the poetry. If expert Romanian-language reports showed the poetry to be of equal weight, I would reconsider the wording.

responses.point: Olsson ranked Carson outside his eight. He holds that formal hybridity can be hard to separate from gesture, and that the book-object dimension of Nox does not carry in translation. He asked which works I think carry the Carson claim most firmly.
responses.response: Autobiography of Red and Nox are the works I would put forward. Public knowledge suggests that their invention does real intellectual and emotional work, joining classical scholarship, lyric and narrative, or elegy and the book-object. But two works cannot settle a claim about a whole oeuvre, and I cannot say that the same quality holds across her smaller conventional corpus. Nox is also the work translation carries least well. I therefore keep Carson as an alternative and not as my first choice. Your point about the unity of Cărtărescu's project weighs with me, because a citation for Carson would have to decide among poetry, essay and translation, and I cannot yet state that scope with confidence.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg would centre the citation on the prose project, with the poetry as origin and context. He declines to count length as sustained quality, and he would want expert reports on the Romanian prose before relying on claims about its sentence-level achievement.
responses.response: I agree on all three points, and his citation wording is close to mine. His refusal to let size stand in for sustained quality is the right test for the late novels. Expert reports on the Romanian prose are not available to me in the supplied evidence, so my preference remains provisional. The one thing I would add is that the citation should name the formal architecture. A wording that says only 'visionary' describes the effect and not the achievement, and it would be the hardest part to defend if challenged.

responses.point: Mattson keeps Adonis as a very close second on formal and linguistic achievement. She says her preference for Cărtărescu rests on how confidently each case can be assessed from the available evidence, not on a difference in seriousness.
responses.response: That is the distinction I would draw, and it answers the chair's question on Adonis. It is a difference in the evidence available to the committee, not a difference in the strength of the claim as I understand it. Remaking the poetic language of a major tradition is an exceptional claim. The prosody and the dialogue with inherited forms are exactly what I cannot verify without Arabic-language expert accounts. I would not oppose Adonis on literary grounds. If such reports were available and confirmed the claim, I could see placing him first or equal, and I keep him as my first alternative for that reason. His citation should rest on the verse, with the essays named only as related work.

responses.point: Sward treats her preference as provisional. She says that Orbitor and Solenoid are not sustained merely because they are large, and she wants the citation to name the cumulative architecture and not only the visionary style.
responses.response: I agree, and her caution is the most important qualification in the discussion. My reading of escalation rather than restatement is a judgment from public knowledge, and I have said it cannot be verified from the supplied evidence. Her suggestion on the citation is what I have adopted. If the committee's readers found that the later volumes only restate the early ones, I would weaken my position, and the choice between Cărtărescu and Adonis would become closer for me.

uncertainties: How much of the Romanian prose texture, rhythm and density survives in translation, including Swedish translation, and whether I am overstating the claim by relying on translated editions and secondary description.
Whether the later large works enlarge the project or only restate its motifs. I read escalation of scale and structure from public knowledge, but I have not verified it by reading the whole corpus.
Whether the poetry and early fiction sustain the level of the major novels, which is why I keep them out of the citation scope.
How to weigh Adonis's achievement in Arabic when it can be judged only through translation and secondary accounts. This is an evidence gap for the committee, not a verdict on the claim.
How to compare cross-genre or poetry-centred oeuvres (Carson, Adonis, Zurita) with novel-centred ones under common criteria, and whether Carson's citation scope could be fixed precisely.
I have not read the originals or independently verified any source. My statements rest on the shortlist descriptions, public knowledge and colleagues' round-1 accounts.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile, which records no personal or professional tie to any shortlisted writer. My own fiction and my Lagerlöf biography are context and not evidence of preference for any candidate. My Academy remarks on a different laureate reflect a collective position and are not my own view of this shortlist. I note the conflict disclosures in other members' round-1 files and the chair summary, including those of Carlberg, Sem-Sandberg and Olsson, and I take them as stated without verifying or adjudicating them. Carlberg's actual committee voting status is undocumented, and her simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
